subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw make non-thread persistent native and ACP `sessions_spawn` sessions a first-class supported contract, and if so what routing and lifecycle semantics should they have?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes session ownership, message routing, cleanup, and ACP delivery behavior rather than repairing a narrowly broken implementation.

options.title: Define non-thread persistence
options.body: Approve a first-class contract for unbound persistent sessions and require one implementation that updates runtime, schema, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Keep session thread-bound
options.body: Leave `mode="session"` tied to thread binding and close or narrow this request toward docs and supported `mode="run"`/`sessions_send` guidance.

options.title: Split ACP and native paths
options.body: Handle ACP persistent affinity through a separate `affinityKey`-style contract while deciding native subagent persistence later.

recommendation.title: Define non-thread persistence
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class contract for unbound persistent sessions and require one implementation that updates runtime, schema, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The current core thread-binding refactor and recent ACP/subagent spawn maintenance point to this handle as the best available routing owner for the product-contract decision.
